items.text: The Supreme Court will hold a special sitting on Sunday, 11 October. A bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana will hear the petition of TMC MP Menaka Guruswamy challenging the preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers, along with a contempt petition over the metro shutdown.
The CJP's legal head called the detention of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and the other protesters illegal and appealed to the Supreme Court to intervene.

Citing officials, Outlook says more than 7,000 protesters were detained in Delhi, and FIRs may be filed over the alleged assault on police personnel. Other reports put the figure between 3,000 and 4,500.
AISA president Neha Bora was released. Other women protesters held at Maidan Garhi police station were also let go.
Arvind Kejriwal, Sanjay Singh and Durgesh Pathak released. In a video, Kejriwal told the Prime Minister that your jails will fall short, and reiterated the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Rahul Gandhi alleged that police and BJP workers beat up students, the city was shut down and the Prime Minister is fighting to save his chair.

The DCP of the North district said pickets are deployed at entry and exit points, Section 163 of the BNSS is in force and no permission has been given for the protest.
The Home Ministry has made available 221 companies of Central armed forces, about 23,000 personnel, in Delhi for 8 to 12 October.
